body:
## Scope

Fix the intermittent shared actionlint installer failure consumed by roughly 18 repositories. Replace the pipe-to-shell installer with a direct download of actionlint 1.7.12 using bounded retries and a SHA-256 checksum pinned in the workflow. Sweep every reusable workflow and composite action in this repository for `bash <(curl` and unverified curl/wget-to-shell patterns; make no unrelated shared-workflow changes.

## Why

The current process substitution can execute a truncated installer script, and that installer performs a second unretried, unchecked archive download. Wave 2 saw four corrupt/truncated archive failures in polylens2otel.

## Acceptance

- [x] `ACTIONLINT_VERSION` remains pinned to 1.7.12
- [x] The Linux x86_64 tarball is downloaded directly with `curl --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 2 --fail`
- [x] A checksum pinned in the workflow is verified before extraction
- [x] The actionlint job remains non-gating
- [x] `rg 'bash <\\(curl|curl.*\\| *(ba)?sh'` returns no matches
- [x] Every workflow and composite action inspected is enumerated, including clean files
- [x] Local actionlint and zizmor validation pass

comments.body:
Sweep denominator: 13 files inspected. The only vulnerable occurrence was `.github/workflows/actionlint.yml`; the other 12 were clean for `bash <(curl`, curl-to-shell and wget-to-shell patterns.

- `.github/actions/bao-secret/action.yml`
- `.github/actions/broker-token/action.yml`
- `.github/workflows/actionlint.yml`
- `.github/workflows/binaries.yml`
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- `.github/workflows/codeql.yml`
- `.github/workflows/container-publish.yml`
- `.github/workflows/dependency-review.yml`
- `.github/workflows/docker-security.yml`
- `.github/workflows/release-please.yml`
- `.github/workflows/scorecard-analysis.yml`
- `.github/workflows/scorecard.yml`
- `.github/workflows/zizmor.yml`

The official v1.7.12 checksum file gives `8aca8db9…a3d8` for `actionlint_1.7.12_linux_amd64.tar.gz`; an independent download matched that SHA-256 and contained the expected `actionlint` member. Local actionlint and zizmor passed. The Linux binary was not executed on macOS; subsequent real Linux caller runs are the runtime proof.

Completed by 328bc72e11165b582079d424fd6b551221435250, pushed directly to main with `Closes #46`. GitHub did not auto-close the issue despite the correctly formatted footer; published history is preserved and this is closed manually under the recovery rule.

body:
`container-publish.yml` builds the main-snapshot chart version as
`0.0.0-main.t<unix-ts>.<shortsha>` (line 392). When a commit's first 12 hex characters happen to be
**all decimal digits and start with `0`**, that last identifier is an invalid semver prerelease and
`helm package` refuses to build the chart:

```
Error: version segment starts with 0
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

Semver: a dot-separated prerelease identifier consisting **only of digits** is a *numeric* identifier,
and numeric identifiers MUST NOT have leading zeros. `097152733415` is all digits with a leading zero,
so the version is malformed. Any identifier containing a hex letter is *alphanumeric*, where leading
zeros are fine — which is why this has been invisible until now.

The comment directly above the line already knows about this class of problem: the `t` prefix on the
timestamp is there "to keep the prerelease identifier alphanumeric". The SHA identifier never got the
same treatment.

## Evidence

Hit live on `rknightion/tailscale2otel@0971527`
([run 30120683193](https://github.com/rknightion/tailscale2otel/actions/runs/30120683193)) — the
`edge (:main image + helm) / helm publish` job failed at *Package and push chart* while every other job
succeeded, and it failed identically on re-run. Reproduced locally with the same helm the action
installs (v4.2.3):

```console
$ helm package <chart> --version "0.0.0-main.t1753387000.097152733415"
Error: version segment starts with 0

$ helm package <chart> --version "0.0.0-main.t1753387000.g097152733415"
Successfully packaged chart ...
```

Roughly 1 commit in 1,800 draws a SHA that trips it — `(1/16) × (10/16)^11` for a leading `0`
followed by eleven more decimal digits. Rare enough to look like a flake, frequent enough to keep
recurring across a fleet.

## Blast radius

Every repo consuming this workflow that publishes a chart: `.github`, `fleet-management-operator`,
`genai-otel-bridge`, `graph2otel`, `meraki-dashboard-exporter`, `opnsense-exporter`,
`paperless-ngx-dedupe`, `sagemcom-f3896-py`, `sf2loki`, `synthkit`, `tailscale2otel`,
`transceiver-exporter`. The failure mode is the same everywhere: the image publishes, the chart does
not, and the next commit silently "fixes" it — so it reads as an infrastructure flake rather than a
bug, and nobody chases it.

Consumers pin this workflow by SHA, so the fix reaches them only as they bump the pin.

## Fix

Prefix the SHA identifier the same way the timestamp already is (`g`, the git-describe convention):

```bash
version="0.0.0-main.t$(date +%s).g${short}"
```

Ordering is unaffected: prerelease comparison is field-by-field, and the timestamp field precedes the
SHA field, so it decides every comparison between two distinct publishes. `appversion` needs no change
— `main-` already makes it alphanumeric, and it is not semver-validated.

One thing to be aware of: anything parsing a 12-hex-char SHA out of the chart *version* string would
need to allow the `g`. The image reference and `appVersion` are unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The main-snapshot chart version is valid semver for **every** possible commit SHA
- [ ] The reason is written down at the line, so the next edit does not undo it
- [ ] Newest-wins ordering for an ArgoCD semver-range `targetRevision` still holds
title: container-publish: an all-numeric short SHA makes the main chart version invalid semver

body:
Follow-on to #14. Five `chore(deps)` action bumps merged before the renovate `build(deps)` fix landed and are still missing from the open release PR #12 (`release 1.4.1`), because `chore` is `hidden: true` in release-please-config.json.

Rewriting those merged commits on `main` is off the table (published history). The clean way to make release-please retroactively wrap them into PR #12 is to **un-hide `chore`** - release-please re-scans all commits since v1.4.0 on the next run and will render the chore commits under a visible section.

Note: `ci` is already non-hidden (Build & CI) - it is what cut 1.4.1 - so no change needed there.

## Implication (intended)
Un-hiding `chore` makes chore commits both **visible in the changelog** and **release-triggering**. For this shared-workflows hub that is desired (consumers pin to release SHAs), but it does mean routine chores will now cut patch releases.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `chore` is non-hidden in release-please-config.json (visible Miscellaneous section)
- [ ] After the RP run, release PR #12 lists the 5 `chore(deps)` docker/codeql action bumps
- [ ] Version stays 1.4.1 (chore is patch-level; ci already forced patch)

comments.body: Done in `d365eee`. Un-hid `chore` in release-please-config.json; the RP run re-scanned and release PR #12 now wraps in all five previously-missing action bumps under a new **Miscellaneous** section (docker/build-push, login, metadata, setup-buildx, github/codeql-action). Version held at 1.4.1 as expected. `ci` was already non-hidden so no change there.

title: release-please: un-hide chore so already-merged action bumps land in the release PR

body:
Renovate opens its GitHub-Actions update PRs with the default `chore(deps):` commit type. In this repo `chore` maps to a `hidden: true` changelog section (release-please-config.json), and release-please treats a commit set whose types are all hidden as **non-releasing** — so those merges run release-please (green) but never create/update the release PR.

## Evidence
- Release PR #12 (`chore(main): release 1.4.1`) last updated `2026-07-03T11:09:44Z`, body lists only the two `ci:` commits.
- Five Renovate merges landed 11:13–11:14 (`chore(deps): update docker/*`, `github/codeql-action`). Their release-please runs all show `success` but the PR was not updated — because `chore` is hidden.
- By contrast `ci:` commits (non-hidden `Build & CI` section) DID cut 1.4.1, proving non-hidden section types trigger a patch bump here.

## Impact
This is a shared-workflows hub: consumers pin the reusables to release SHAs and Renovate bumps them when a new release lands. Action bumps to the reusables therefore sit on `main` untagged and invisible in the changelog until some unrelated `feat`/`fix`/`ci` commit happens to sweep them into a release.

## Fix
Override the Renovate commit type for dependency updates in this repo to a non-hidden, releasable conventional type (`build`), so each action bump proactively opens/updates the release PR and shows under **Build & CI**. Scope to this repo via `renovate.json` packageRules; the fleet `config.js` default (`chore`) stays for app repos where action bumps should not cut releases.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `renovate.json` sets `semanticCommitType: build` for `github-actions` (and the goreleaser custom manager) updates
- [ ] Next Renovate action bump commits as `build(deps): ...` and release-please opens/updates the release PR to include it
- [ ] The bump appears under the Build & CI changelog section

comments.body: Fixed in `de5c667`. Added a repo-scoped `renovate.json` packageRule setting `semanticCommitType: build` / `semanticCommitScope: deps` for the `github-actions` and `custom.regex` (goreleaser) managers. Renovate action bumps now commit as `build(deps): ...` - a non-hidden, releasable type - so release-please opens/updates the release PR on each merge and lists them under Build & CI. Config validated with `renovate-config-validator` (Config validated successfully). Fleet `config.js` default (`chore`) untouched for app repos.

title: Renovate action-update merges don't trigger a release-please release

body:
## Problem

`.github` is the only rknightion repo where Renovate opens PRs but never platform-automerges them. Open PRs (#7–#11, all `app/rknightion-renovate`) sit with `autoMergeRequest=null`. Renovate's `platformAutomerge` (inherited from the fleet `renovate-config` via autodiscover) tries to arm GitHub native auto-merge but can't, because the repo lacks the settings/ruleset the rest of the fleet has.

## Root cause — `.github` diverges from every other repo on three counts

| setting | `.github` | rest of fleet (synthkit, meraki, opnsense, tailscale2otel, …) |
|---|---|---|
| `allow_auto_merge` | **false** | true |
| `delete_branch_on_merge` | **false** | true |
| `main` branch ruleset | **absent** | active, requires `ci-success` status check |

GitHub won't arm auto-merge on a branch with no required checks, so both the ruleset *and* `allow_auto_merge` are needed. The Renovate config side is already correct (policy inherited from `renovate-config` config.js).

## Plan / acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add a `ci-success` aggregator job to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (gates on actionlint/zizmor/codeql), matching the fleet idiom — so the required status check actually exists and passes
- [ ] Enable `allow_auto_merge: true` on the repo
- [ ] Enable `delete_branch_on_merge: true` on the repo
- [ ] Create the `main` branch ruleset requiring the `ci-success` check + a PR rule (0 approvals), replicating synthkit's exactly (admin bypass, deletion + non-fast-forward protection)
- [ ] Confirm open Renovate PRs get auto-merge armed on the next Renovate run

Once this lands, the hub behaves like the rest of the fleet: Renovate PRs auto-merge after `ci-success` goes green.

comments.body:
Done — the hub now matches the fleet automerge setup. All four criteria landed:

**`ci-success` aggregator job** — added to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` in `4369add` (gates on actionlint/zizmor/codeql, `if: always()`, same idiom as synthkit). This is the single required check.

**Repo settings** (no git trace, applied via API):
- `allow_auto_merge`: false → **true**
- `delete_branch_on_merge`: false → **true**

**`main` branch ruleset** — created (id `18475192`), rules verified byte-identical to synthkit's: `ci-success` required status check (integration 15368), PR rule (0 approvals), deletion + non-fast-forward protection, admin (RepositoryRole 5) always-bypass.

Result: `.github` merge settings + ruleset now equal the rest of the fleet.

**Open Renovate PRs (#7–#11):** they were branched before the `ci-success` job existed, so they'll show the check as pending until Renovate rebases them onto the new `main` (which it does automatically on its next run once the base has moved). After the rebase they get `ci-success`, go green, and Renovate arms platform-automerge as it does elsewhere. No manual intervention needed.

title: Enable Renovate platform automerge on the hub repo (match fleet)

body:
## Goal

Roll out OpenSSF Scorecard supply-chain analysis across the whole rknightion public OSS fleet, via the shared reusable-workflow pattern (like `codeql`/`zizmor`), and publish results so each repo gets a [scorecard.dev](https://scorecard.dev) badge.

## Key decisions (settled)

- **Reusable workflow, not per-repo copies.** New `.github/workflows/scorecard.yml` reusable; each repo gets a thin caller pinned to a release SHA. `publish_results` (OIDC) is confirmed to work through inter-repo reusable workflows (verified against ossf/scorecard-webapp source; PRs #295, #778).
- **No PAT.** The fleet enforces branch policy via **Repository Rulesets**, which Scorecard reads with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`. A `repo_token` PAT is only needed for legacy *classic* Branch Protection — which the fleet does not use. Confirmed all 16 public non-fork repos use rulesets (0 classic).
- **Triggers:** `push: [main]` + weekly `schedule` cron only. Dropped the stale `branch_protection_rule` trigger the old standalone files used.
- **Badge domain:** `api.scorecard.dev` / `scorecard.dev` (the old `securityscorecards.dev` is retired).

## Scope

16 public non-fork source repos. Excludes `rknightion/opentelemetry-demo` (a fork — Scorecard unsupported on forks). 5 repos already have a copy-pasted standalone Scorecard workflow (meraki-dashboard-exporter, autopi-ha, kiosker-ha, sf2loki, + the fork) — these get replaced by the thin caller.

## Plan / acceptance criteria

- [x] `scorecard.yml` reusable added to `rknightion/.github` + README documented
- [x] `.github` `v1.4.0` release cut (callers pin to its SHA)
- [x] Thin caller wired into all 16 public repos (replacing the 5 standalone files)
- [x] `scorecard.dev` badge added to each repo README
- [x] `transceiver-exporter` given a matching branch ruleset (it currently has none, so its Branch-Protection check would score low regardless)

## Notes

- `transceiver-exporter` is the only public repo with **no** ruleset — being fixed as part of this so it scores consistently.

comments.body:
## ✅ Rollout complete

Scorecard is live across the whole public fleet.

**Shared reusable:** `rknightion/.github/.github/workflows/scorecard.yml`, released as **`v1.4.0`** (SHA `8718898e512efc196dba6888b7d20d7b21019bf2`). No PAT — publishes via OIDC, reads Rulesets with the default token.

**Wired into 17 public repos** (scope was stated as 16 — the fleet is actually **17** non-fork source repos; all done). Each got a thin `push`+weekly-`schedule` caller pinned to the v1.4.0 SHA, plus a `scorecard.dev` badge in its README:
opnsense-exporter, paperless-ngx-dedupe, grotTrack, robknight-hetzner-datasource, genai-otel-bridge, tailscale2otel, kiosker-ha, fleet-management-operator, autopi-ha, sf2loki, meraki-dashboard-ha, transceiver-exporter, synthkit, sagemcom-f3896-py, bumblebee-catalog, profilarr, meraki-dashboard-exporter.

The 3 pre-existing standalone Scorecard workflows (autopi-ha, kiosker-ha `scorecards.yml`; sf2loki, meraki-dashboard-exporter `scorecard.yml`) were replaced by the caller. `opentelemetry-demo` excluded (fork). Verified: 6+ runs already completed **success**, rest queued/running.

**`transceiver-exporter`** — added a matching 4-rule branch ruleset (it was the only public repo with none), so its Branch-Protection check scores consistently.

## Notes for the record

- **Temporary version skew:** callers pin scorecard@`v1.4.0` while the other shared reusables (codeql/zizmor/etc.) are still pinned at `v1.3.1` in each repo. Renovate owns those bumps and will converge the whole fleet to v1.4.0 on its next run — no action needed.
- **`.github` hub repo** itself is not wired (it's the workflow source). Trivial to add later if wanted.
- Two repos (synthkit, meraki-dashboard-ha) had stray untracked `.codacy/*summary.json` artifacts from a prior Codacy-skill session accidentally swept into the first commit by `git add -A`; both were backed out (untracked, local copies kept) and those repos' CLAUDE.md rules (never `git add -A`) noted.
